newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai sugar premiums firm as demand picks up.
newsitem.headline: Thai sugar premiums firm as demand picks up.

text.p: Thai raw sugar premiums rose over the past week on an Indonesian purchase of up to five sugar cargoes and reports of buying by China, trade sources said on Monday.
Indonesia bought around 60,000 tonnes of white sugar from Thailand for delivery early next year, trade sources added.
Market talk that Russia would soon buy, if it had not already bought, 100,000 tonnes of raws also buoyed Thai prices.
January/March and February/April were quoted at 1.00 cent a pound over New York futures, from 0.85 cent a week ago.
Thai white sugar premiums of 45 ICUMSA for February/March delivery were bid at $4 over London March futures.
"There were some good news this week. But the overall picture remains weak with news on record sugar output," said a trader at a Japanese trading firm.
Traders here and in Hong Kong said they also heard market talk that China had bought a few cargoes of raws but had no idea about origin.
"If they bought, the amount is not likely to be substantial due to big stocks they have built from overbuying last year," said one trader in Hong Kong.
"There has been lots of enquiries from China recently," said another trader.
One Thai trader said he expected Thai premiums to be mostly steady to slightly higher next week.
"Floods and uncertainties over crushing which normally starts in November will support the premiums," one producer said.
"True, last year the flood was more severe and yet we still have good crop. But until a clear picture of flood damage on the crop and crushing schedule emerges, concerns will persist," he said.

At a Thai port, the Xin An Jiang was loading 13,100 tonnes of bagged white sugar to be shipped to Indonesia. Kerry was the buyer, shipping sources said. The vessel was scheduled to be ready on October 15-16.
Orient Express 1 was loading 1,000 tonnes of whites that Tate & Lyle bought to be shipped to Cambodia.
